conversation_snippet:
Alex: What would you say is making it difficult for you to lose 2 stone & keep it off sustainably?
Emma: Honestly it feels like self sabotage. Every time I get some momentum I start comfort eating in the evenings because of work stress.

replies.direct: I hear you Emma, self-sabotage often stems from deeper patterns, and comfort eating from stress is a classic example. Stress is one of the major weight loss inhibiting factors due to changes in cortisol levels. Is your work stress due to your current working role being quite stressful and challenging on a regular basis? Or do you have other responsibilities adding to that pressure?
replies.empathetic: Oh Emma, I really hear you. That feeling of self-sabotage, especially when you're getting momentum, is incredibly frustrating and so many women resonate with that. It's almost like you're fighting against yourself, isn't it? And then coupling that with comfort eating because of work stress just adds another layer. To get a better understanding of what's going on, could you provide some insights about your eating habits? Or what do your daily meals look like? Also, how are your energy levels throughout the day?
replies.short: I hear you Emma. Is that work stress mainly due to your job role, or are there other responsibilities making things tough?

rationale: Emma has identified 'self sabotage' and 'comfort eating' as barriers, explicitly linking the latter to 'work stress'. The direct reply immediately deep-dives into the nature of her stress (following the 'Stress' script) as it's the stated root cause for the comfort eating. The empathetic reply validates her feelings around self-sabotage and the struggle, then broadens the diagnostic to her overall eating habits and energy levels (following the 'Comfort/Boredom Eating' script), which are also influenced by stress. The short reply offers a quick, casual follow-up on the stress component to keep momentum.
